title: Weather, seasons, and small talk
goal: Talk about the weather — the safest way into a conversation with a stranger — and see why Egyptian weather sentences have no subject at all.
bekal: describe the weather and seasons in Egypt and in your own country
open light small talk with someone you don't know
use أوي، جداً، خالص، شوية to set the degree

dialogs.title: حوار — في يوليو
dialogs.intro: The height of the Cairo summer. Budi and Umm Sayed are both sheltering in the building lobby, waiting for the elevator.

lines.speaker: أم سيد:
lines.text: الحر ده مش طبيعي! الجو زي الفرن.
lines.baca: il-harr da mish ṭabii‘i! ig-gaww zayy il-furn.
lines.id: This heat isn't normal! The weather is like an oven.
lines.literal: the-heat this not natural! the-weather like the-oven.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Really. How hot is it today?

lines.speaker: أم سيد:
lines.text: قالوا اتنين وأربعين. وبكرة أسخن كمان.
lines.baca: ’aalu itnēn wi arbi‘iin. wi bukra askhan kamaan.
lines.id: They said forty-two. And tomorrow it'll be even hotter.
lines.literal: they-said two and forty. and tomorrow hotter too.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: ربنا يستر. أنا مش متعود على الجفاف ده.
lines.baca: rabbina yustur. ana mish mit‘awwid ‘alag-gafaaf da.
lines.id: God help us. I'm not used to this dryness.
lines.literal: our-Lord cover. I not used to the-dryness this.

lines.speaker: أم سيد:
lines.id: And what's it like in your country? Hot too?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: حر بس رطب. عندنا مطرة كتير طول السنة.
lines.baca: harr bas raṭb. ‘andina maṭara kitiir ṭuul is-sana.
lines.id: Hot but humid. It rains a lot all year round.
lines.literal: hot but humid. at-us rain much all the-year.

lines.speaker: أم سيد:
lines.text: مطرة طول السنة؟ يا سلام! هنا بتنزل كام مرة بس.
lines.baca: maṭara ṭuul is-sana? ya salaam! hina bitinzil kaam marra bas.
lines.id: Rain all year round? Wow! Here it only falls a few times.
lines.literal: rain all the-year? O peace! here it-falls how-many time only.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: وفي الشتا الجو بيبرد أوي هنا؟
lines.id: And in winter, does it get very cold here?
lines.literal: and in-the-winter the-weather it-gets-cold very here?

lines.speaker: أم سيد:
lines.text: بيبرد، بس مش زي بره. عشر درجات كده.
lines.baca: biybrad, bas mish zayy barra. ‘ashar daragaat kida.
lines.id: It gets cold, but not like abroad. About ten degrees.
lines.literal: it-gets-cold, but not like outside. ten degrees like-that.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: That's not cold at all for us!

lines.speaker: أم سيد:
lines.text: هههه، المصريين بيلبسوا جواكت في عشر درجات.
lines.baca: hahaha, il-maṣriyyiin biylbisu gawakit fi ‘ashar daragaat.
lines.id: Hahaha, Egyptians wear jackets at ten degrees.
lines.literal: hahaha, the-Egyptians they-wear jackets at ten degrees.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: And what's the best time of year?

lines.speaker: أم سيد:
lines.baca: uktōbar wi nufimbir. ig-gaww biyib’a tuhfa.
lines.id: October and November. The weather gets amazing.
lines.literal: October and November. the-weather it-becomes masterpiece.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: يبقى لازم أستنى. المصعد جه أهو.
lines.baca: yib’a laazim astanna. il-maṣ‘ad gih ahu.
lines.id: Then I'll have to wait. Oh, here's the elevator.
lines.literal: so must I-wait. the-elevator came here-it-is.

lines.speaker: أم سيد:
lines.text: اتفضل يا ابني. وخد معاك مية، الجو خطر.
lines.baca: itfaḍḍal ya ibni. wi khud ma‘aak mayya, ig-gaww khaṭar.
lines.id: After you, son. And take water with you, the weather is dangerous.
lines.literal: go-ahead O my-son. and take with-you water, the-weather danger.

notes: **Egyptian weather sentences have no dummy subject.** English has to say "it is hot", with an it that points to nothing; Egyptian just says الجو حر ("the weather is hot") or simply حر. Think of it as English "hot today!", minus the "it's".
**The word جو means weather and also atmosphere.** الجو حلو can mean "the weather is nice" or "the vibe is nice". For a party or a place: الجو هنا تحفة.
**The word برضه means "too" or "still, anyway", and it is very Egyptian.** أنا برضه رايح (I'm going anyway), وانت برضه؟ (you too?). Few words make your speech sound Egyptian faster.

**The phrase يا سلام expresses amazement**, literally "O peace". It's used for things that impress you and — with a different tone — for things that annoy you. Its relatives: يا نهار أبيض (good grief) and ربنا يستر (God help us).

**The word متعود means "used to", and it is an active participle like those in unit seventeen.** مش متعود (not used to it), متعودة (feminine), متعودين (plural). The verb is اتعود, and حتتعود means you'll get used to it.

**The word بيبقى means "becomes, gets", and it is used constantly.** الجو بيبقى تحفة (the weather gets amazing), يبقى لازم أستنى (so I have to wait). At the start of a conclusion, يبقى means "so" or "then".

grammars.title: Setting the degree: a bit, a lot, very
body: Egyptian has a handful of intensifiers and softeners, and each has its own fixed spot that can't be swapped.
after: Notice that **they all stand after** the word they modify, never before. That is the opposite of English "very hot" — more like "hot indeed".
The word خالص has two faces: after a negative it means "at all", while after a positive sentence it means "really, totally": تعبان خالص (totally exhausted).
The word شوية also means "a moment" for time: استنى شوية (wait a moment). Its more casual cousin: حبة, from the word for "grain".

grammars.title: Weather and seasons
body: Most weather sentences use الجو + adjective, and a few use a verb.
after: Notice that for rain and sunshine the subject is not الجو but **الدنيا** — "the world". This is a fixed habit and can't be swapped: الدنيا بتمطر is right, while الجو بيمطر sounds odd.
The word الدنيا is also used for the general state of things: الدنيا زحمة (it's really crowded), الدنيا هدية دلوقتي (things are calm now), إيه الدنيا؟ (how's the world treating you?).

sections.title: Small talk that never goes wrong

blocks.text: Small talk in Egypt rarely starts with the weather alone. It is usually a short chain: greeting, how are you, how's the family, a grumble about the weather or prices, and only then the actual business.

head: مصري
Say it
Meaning
rows: how are you? how's it going?
what's the weather like where you are?

blocks.text: The phrase الدنيا غالية أوي is Egypt's national complaint, and bringing it up is the quickest way to find common ground with someone you've just met. The reply is almost always ربنا يسهل or الحمد لله على كل حال — a pair of phrases that accept things as they are without giving in to them.

blocks.title: How long small talk should last
items: In Egypt, jumping straight to business without small talk feels like cutting in line. A rule of thumb: at least three turns of talk before you mention what you need.
On the other hand, small talk doesn't mean the whole conversation must be long. After three or four turns, you can say على فكرة *‘ala fikra* ("by the way") and get to the point.
If you're really in a hurry: أنا آسف، أنا مستعجل شوية *ana musta‘gil shuwayya*. It's understood and won't offend.

blocks.text: The word قمر means moon, and Egyptians use it as a compliment for someone beautiful or good-looking: يا قمر. The same word gives the term "moon letters" you met in unit three — letters that don't absorb the l of الـ, as in القمر itself.

items: I'm not used to this heat.
Where I'm from it's hot but humid.

exercises.prompt: Answer each question about your own country in one Egyptian Arabic sentence.
Put the words in the right order.
items: الجفاف / متعود / مش / ده / على / أنا

answers: الجو حر أوي النهاردة. — الدنيا بتمطر. — النهاردة كام درجة؟ — أنا مش متعود على الحر ده. — عندنا حر بس رطب.
الجو حر ورطب. — أيوه، بيمطر كتير أوي. — لأ، مافيش شتا عندنا. — أحسن وقت يونيو ويوليو. — الجو رطب أوي.
الحر ده مش طبيعي. — النهاردة كام درجة؟ — أنا مش متعود على الجفاف ده. — عندنا مطرة كتير طول السنة. — في أكتوبر الجو بيبقى تحفة.
